items.descriptionOriginal: Dietary guidelines seem to run the gamut depending on where you live. In Japan, grain-based dishes are the main focus, while Greece promotes the Mediterranean diet and the U.S. emphasizes protein . So nutrition scientists from around the globe recently came together to develop a compendium of advice that’s adaptable across cultures (and takes the health of the planet into account). Enter: the International Food Guide Pyramid. The team compared national and regional dietary guidelines from the United States, Canada, Germany, Australia, China, the Netherlands, and the Nordic countries, in addition to analyzing more than 250 scientific publications, to pinpoint the shared fundamentals of healthy eating. As it turns out, they may be more universal than it often seems. “Despite what people often hear, there’s actually substantial agreement in nutrition science about the foundations of healthy eating,” study lead Karen Della Corte said in a news release. She added that a balanced diet will look different for each person, so the guidelines are designed to be adjusted to include local, affordable, and culturally appropriate foods. The new food pyramid focuses on plant foods, healthier sources of fat and protein, and high-quality carbohydrates. At the base — representing the foundation of a nourishing diet — are vegetables and fruit as well as whole and low-glycemic index grains. Above that are plant-based proteins like beans, nuts, and seeds, as well as plant-based oils. Next up are fish, poultry, eggs, and certain dairy products, and at the top, for use sparingly, are refined grains, red and processed meats, butter, chips, sugary drinks and snacks, and salt. A 2025 report from the EAT-Lancet commission called for similarly plant-forward international guidelines, suggesting they could prevent 15 million premature deaths per year and reduce environmental impacts like greenhouse gas emissions. “Our diet has to be not only for our own health but also for the health of our planet,” said David Jenkins of the University of Toronto, creator of the glycemic index. “Our science base has to be appropriately comprehensive to include that.” Karen Della Corte Corte offered the following advice for putting the pyramid’s principles into practice: Design your meal around the plant food you want to emphasize, first thinking about which vegetables, whole grains, beans, or lentils you could include. Opt for beans, peas, lentils, fish, poultry, or yogurt more frequently than red or processed meats, and don’t make meat the biggest part of any meal. Reach for snacks like nuts, seeds, fruit, or vegetables with hummus over less nutritious processed options. Choose whole-grain bread over refined white bread and whole-grain or high-fiber cereals rather than refined, puffed, flaked, or popped cereals. Use canola or olive oil in your cooking instead of animal fats like butter or tallow. Drink water instead of soda.

Τα δεκάλεπτα: 14-22, 31-35, 45-53, 58-77. Οι «ερυθρόλευκες», που ουσιαστικά κλείδωσαν απόψε την πρόκριση στην επόμενη φάση, βρέθηκαν πίσω στο σκορ στο πρώτο μέρος, με την ισπανική ομάδα να προηγείται με 35-31 στην ανάπαυλα. Η Χριστινάκη ήταν η κορυφαία του Ολυμπιακού με 19 πόντους, 9 ριμπάουντ και 3 ασίστ, ενώ η Φάνκαμ πρόσθεσε 13 πόντους και 12 ριμπάουντ. Για την Μπάξι Φερόλ, η Ντούγκαν σημείωσε επίσης 19 πόντους. items.descriptionOriginal: Choosing the right treatment for a child with a malignant brain tumor requires a careful balance. Therapy must be strong enough to keep the cancer from coming back, but it can also cause lasting side effects that affect learning, development and quality of life. Now, an international team led by researchers at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute has developed an artificial intelligence model that may help doctors make those decisions with greater precision.

items.descriptionOriginal: Hyundai-backed Boston Dynamics has unveiled Stretch Gen 2, a next-generation autonomous robot designed to unload trailers faster and reduce maintenance downtime in high-volume logistics operations. Built on data from more than 100,000 operating hours and tens of millions of boxes unloaded by its predecessor, the upgraded robot features a redesigned gripper, improved sensing, 81 percent less internal cabling, and modular components that allow faster repairs. The changes are aimed at preventing mechanical wear and electrical faults that could take the robot offline. Boston Dynamics has also redesigned its exterior panels to withstand falling boxes and repositioned the emergency stop button to reduce accidental safety stoppages. “Our customers count on Stretch to keep freight moving, and every hour a robot sits idle is an hour of work that piles up on the dock,” said Brian Donnelly, Vice President & General Manager of Logistics Robotics at Boston Dynamics. “With Gen 2, we focused on the things that actually took robots offline in the real world. We made it tougher, we made it simpler to service, and we made sure it keeps getting better long after it’s deployed.” Faster repairs keep robots working The redesigned robot also aims to make maintenance less time-consuming when components need replacement. Boston Dynamics said a complete swerve drive swap now takes about one hour, compared with an entire day previously. The company has removed dynamic cables and complex wiring harnesses, replacing them with a simpler architecture and standardized high-strength fasteners. These changes are intended to reduce the number of tools required during repairs and shorten the time technicians spend working on the machine. Stretch Gen 2 also includes onboard diagnostics and maintenance tools that allow customers’ own maintenance teams to handle more routine servicing. This could reduce dependence on external support and help keep robots operating on busy warehouse docks. Software updates improve performance Beyond its mechanical changes, Stretch Gen 2 runs on a redesigned onboard computing platform that supports continuous software improvements. Boston Dynamics said regular software releases will improve case detection, motion planning, picking strategies and world modeling across deployed robot fleets. These updates can deliver performance improvements without requiring customers to replace or upgrade the robot’s physical hardware. The robot can unload up to 1,000 cases per hour, although actual throughput depends on factors such as box weight and how neatly or irregularly packages are stacked inside trailers. A multipick feature allows it to handle multiple boxes in a single picking cycle to reach higher throughput rates. Its battery is designed to last two work shifts, while a fast charger can restore the charge to 90 percent in approximately 75 minutes. Onboard lighting also allows the robot to operate inside dark trailers, where visibility can be limited. Stretch comes with a pre-trained vision system that can identify most packages from the first day of deployment without requiring additional programming. Boston Dynamics has positioned Stretch as a solution for automating one of the more physically demanding tasks in logistics . Trailer unloading involves handling large volumes of packages in confined spaces, often under varying lighting conditions and with boxes stacked in unpredictable arrangements. The second-generation model builds on the company’s existing deployments, with a stronger focus on reliability, serviceability, and sustained performance in demanding warehouse environments.

items.descriptionOriginal: A maker who goes by Max Imagination has built a 70-gram remote-controlled butterfly. The project is called ESP-FLUTTER. The butterfly flies by flapping two wings, each driver by its own servo, a small motor that turns to set angles, a Hackster report said. The wings are thin plastic from produce bags stretched over carbon-fiber frames, and 50 small LEDs light them for night flights. ESP-FLUTTER is an ornithopter, an aircraft that gets lift and thrust from flapping wings instead of propellers. Many ornithopters use one motor and a mechanical linkage to move both wings. This design uses two independent servos, which Hackster said gives more control while keeping the mechanics simple. A Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3, a small development board, handles the servo signals, wireless link, battery monitoring and LEDs. Max Imagination posted the firmware on GitHub and build files on Google Drive, so other builders can start from the same design. Built to stay light Most flying robots use spinning propellers , which is easier than flapping a pair of wings, according to the Hackster report . Weight is a major concern, so the whole aircraft stays at 70 grams with its battery, the video description says. The 3D-printed frame is PETG plastic, with flexible TPU guards that protect the servos in crashes. Carbon-fiber rods give the wings structure without much weight. The wing film is thin plastic from produce bags, secured with flexible adhesive, and lightweight kite fabric is another option. Hackster said the design uses no exotic materials or costly components. Power comes from a custom two-cell lithium-polymer battery pack. A pair of high-speed servos does the flapping, since ordinary hobby servos aren’t fast or powerful enough. Max Imagination wired the 50 LEDs around the wings with extremely thin enameled copper wire, which adds about 1 gram to each wing. Hackster said two versions exist: a modular one built from easy-to-find parts and a compact one built around a custom four-layer circuit board, a flat panel that links the electronics. Phone controls and limits The pilot connects a phone to the butterfly’s own Wi-Fi network and opens a browser-based control page. An optional ExpressLRS receiver lets a standard radio transmitter fly it instead. The page adjusts flapping frequency, steering response, servo positions, and wing motion profiles. A sine wave, which rises and falls smoothly, gives more natural-looking movement, while a triangle wave can produce more lift. Max Imagination found that about 4 hertz, or four flaps per second, works well at full throttle. The maker’s YouTube description lists a longest flight of 1 minute, 9 seconds and a range of about 25 meters. Both figures are self-reported. No outside test or other builder’s results are cited, so real-world performance is unproven. Independent flight times from builders using the GitHub files would show how practical the design is. Max Imagination said a controller setup video is coming. Max Imagination posted the build video on Oct. 16, and Hackster reported on it.

Η λαμπερή μπαλάντα είναι πλέον ένα τυπικό που ακούγεται εύκολα, αλλά ο Joel δεν την άρεσε όταν την έγραψε. Μάλιστα, σκέφτηκε να το αφήσει από το άλμπουμ του The Stranger μέχρι τη Linda Ronstadt…
items.descriptionOriginal: It’s often easier to spot genius in others than in ourselves, and the story of how Billy Joel ‘s “Just the Way You Are” almost didn’t get recorded is a perfect example. The lilting ballad is now an easy-listening standard, but Joel wasn’t fond of it when he wrote it. In fact, he considered leaving it off his album The Stranger until Linda Ronstadt heard it and changed his mind. View this post on Instagram ‘Are you out of your mind?’ Joel shared the story in a recent interview with Rick Beato : “The first really big hit I had was a song called ‘Just the Way You Are,’ which was a ballad,” Joel said. “I didn’t even want to put it on the album cuz I thought it was…too soft, too mushy. Linda Ronstadt and Phoebe Snow were in the studio, and we played the song for them. I said, ‘I don’t like this song that much.’ Linda Ronstadt goes, ‘Are you out of your mind? That’s a hit record! You got to put that on the album. That’s a great song.’ She talked me into it. So, I have to thank Linda Ronstadt for that song.” We all have to thank Linda Ronstadt. “Just the Way You Are” became one of Joel’s most beloved and top-performing hits . It’s also a near-perfect love song. What woman doesn’t want to be told that she doesn’t need to change herself in any way, that she is loved just as she is? Mercy, the lyrics alone are worth the Grammys it won for Song of the Year and Record of the Year in 1978. It’s the song Paul McCartney said he wished he’d written Joel really didn’t know the gem he had in his hands with that song. Not only did Linda Ronstadt love it, but Paul McCartney himself said he wished he had written it. “When I first heard Billy, it was like, ‘Oh, wait a minute. He’s good. Who’s this?'” McCartney said in the HBO Max documentary, Billy Joel: And So It Goes . “You know, like you do, your ears prick up. The song that really made me know that that was happening was ‘Just the Way You Are.’ And where I get asked, ‘Is there a song that you wish you’d written?’ And I always … that’s the one I always say.” Imagine Paul McCartney saying he wished he’d written a song you wrote. You can’t get a pop music compliment higher than that. “That blew me away,” Joel told Beato. “I mean, that’s amazing. And he’s like the melodic king. He can do no wrong with melody.” It almost sounds like a McCartney melody when you think about it. No wonder he wishes he’d written it. Sorry you didn’t like it, Billy, because so many people do Joel wrote the song for his first wife and business manager, Elizabeth Weber. Unfortunately, the couple divorced in 1982. Joel would later remark that his love songs seemed to curse his relationships, and he rarely played “Just the Way You Are” live after his early concerts. However, many people have shared that they played the song at their weddings and had long, happy marriages. And praise for the song still shines nearly 50 years after it was written: “A special love I had with someone…we broke up and he won me back by singing this song.” “Still one of the most beautiful love songs ever written!” “I mean, this is what every woman wants to hear. Thank you.” “This track has aged better than a fine wine, absolute classic.” “A masterpiece of a song. I’ve been married 37 years now and appreciate this song more than ever today.” “Our wedding dance song from 1982 still chills me…all these 40 years of married bliss!” You can watch Beato’s full interview with Billy Joel here: The post Billy Joel thought ‘Just the Way You Are’ was ‘too mushy’ and wanted to nix it. Linda Ronstadt changed his mind. appeared first on Upworthy .

Το μόνο πρόβλημα είναι ότι δεν είναι αληθινός. Και ούτε αυτή είναι η συνταγή…
items.descriptionOriginal: You’re scrolling through your Facebook, Instagram , or TikTok feed when a strikingly handsome food influencer catches your eye. He’s in the kitchen mixing ingredients , explaining the nutritional benefits of each, and making a delicious-looking, healthy recipe you definitely want to try. The only problem is, he’s not real. And neither is that recipe. A loved one recently sent me a Facebook Reel from an account called Nico Reeves Health. The page has 17,000 Facebook followers. The person who sent it to me thought the recipe looked “Yum.” But to me, it felt “off.” View this post on Instagram The guy was too beautiful. The finished recipe looked too perfect. I checked out a few other videos on the Facebook account , and it quickly became clear that the entire account was AI-generated. I found an Instagram account with the same name that has only eight followers and a few videos. On Instagram, the account profile is clearly labeled as AI-generated. On the Facebook page, it is not. The Facebook video I was sent has over 865,000 views—quite a revenue generator for the account. But it’s fake, fake, fake. How to spot an AI-generated account Many of these videos have an “AI content” label, but most people won’t assume that means the entire account is AI-generated. In the early days of AI content, it was pretty easy to spot when an image or video was fake. People in them had extra fingers and limbs, faces didn’t look real, and so on. Now, AI-generated people may look slightly too perfect, but even that’s changing. It’s getting harder and harder to tell whether a person in a video is real, and it’s only going to get more difficult. Some people insist they can tell when a person is AI-generated by their eyes. That may be true most of the time, but AI-generated people are becoming more realistic every day. There’s still a slightly uncanny quality to AI-generated people, something that’s hard to pinpoint but just feels “off,” but how much longer will that be the case? Another AI-generated health account, Marlon Cade Health on TikTok, is quite convincing at first blush. Check this out: The TikTok profile says Cade is a “Retired NFL Nutritionist” who shares “Simple habits. Real food. Better living.” The page has over 200,000 followers. The profile doesn’t mention AI use, but individual videos include a note that says “Creator labeled as AI-generated.” Still, many people in the comments can’t tell that the guy himself isn’t a real human. At this point, it’s not the “people” in these videos, but everything else that provides the clearest AI “tells.” Here’s what to look for: The devil’s in the (background) details When we look past the person and focus on the background in these videos, especially across multiple clips, it becomes much clearer that they are AI-generated. Every Nico Reeves video has an American flag in the background, but in a couple of videos, there are two U.S. flags , one right on top of the other. That alone is weird. But if you look at the bottom flag, the number of stars is wrong. In the first video in this article, the flag behind the speaker only has 11 stripes instead of 13, like a real flag. AI struggles to consistently get the flag right. Another big tell is the kitchen itself. In some videos, the cabinets are green; in some, they’re white; in some, they’re oak. Countertops change, too. In the Marlon Cade videos, small inconsistencies in his tattoos, both within and between videos, are a dead giveaway. The details in his intricate right arm sleeve change, and some small tattoos on his left arm or chest appear and disappear at different times. You wouldn’t notice it unless you looked for it. (And judging by many commenters, they’re too busy gazing at his beautiful eyes to notice much else.) Looking around throughout each video and comparing details across them is key to spotting an entirely AI account. The problem with AI-generated ‘health’ accounts Another big giveaway with these accounts, once you watch enough videos, is how unrealistic many of the recipes and other food tips are. Some are perfectly fine, but others don’t really make sense, and the finished product definitely would not come out the way they show. Of course, there’s a lot of conflicting health and nutrition information out there anyway, but when an account is entirely AI-generated, where is the accountability? These accounts claim to be sharing how food affects health, immunity, longevity, and more, but in reality, they’re money-making machines. Not only do they generate revenue with video views (the Marlon Cade Health account has many videos with hundreds of thousands and even millions of views), but they also direct-message commenters who respond with the prompt word (such as “yes” or “recipe”) to get them into a sales funnel for books, subscriptions, and more. It’s one thing for an actual nutritionist to create real videos to sell a real product. It’s entirely another for who-knows-who with who-knows-what credentials to create an AI-generated account to sell a product that is most likely also AI-generated. Sure, it’s grifty, but it could also be unsafe. I don’t love giving these accounts more views by sharing them, but we’ll be seeing more and more as AI gets more convincing. It’s good to know what to watch for in the meantime, and to share this information with our loved ones so they don’t find themselves duped. The post Entire social media ‘health’ channels are now completely AI-generated. Here’s how to spot them. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: It’s a rite of passage at every school: kids fight with their parents over what to wear, frantic moms accommodate last-minute hair styling requests, and everyone flashes their most mediocre smiles to be immortalized forever. Yes, it’s school picture day , and almost all parents agree it’s a total scam. Mom perfectly captures the lunacy of school photo packages Annie Laferriere is a popular creator with over 50 thousand followers on Instagram. She shares skits and observations about the often-hilarious side of parenting. In one recent video, she took the opportunity to skewer, in comedic fashion, the absolutely antiquated and nonsensical process of ordering school photos. It’s a conundrum most parents are all-too-familiar with. “Hi, I wanted to buy school photos for my kids,” she says to an imaginary conversation partner. “I think I just want the digital.” Laferriere, also playing the role of representative from the photography company, responds snidely, “You’re gonna need some wallets, aren’t you?” “I don’t keep photos in a wallet. I just want the digital.” “You can’t just have a digital,” she responds to herself. “You have to have the package. The package starts at $39, and then you add on the digital. …And for that, you’ll pay dearly.” The exchange continues and becomes increasingly unhinged before Laferriere gives in. “Just give me the wallets. I’ll buy the wallet thingy.” View this post on Instagram Parents agree, school photo packages are out of control It’s a common lament. School picture day photos often aren’t great; the packages are extremely inconvenient, and prices have been soaring for years. Hundreds of commenters chimed in on Laferriere’s post to express their own frustrations: “75 bucks for the digital of 4 mediocre pics… my son isn’t mediocre but takes the moooooost mid photos bc he has not yet found his comfort zone at picture day and doesn’t give a real smile … well get there one day” “Hilarious that they still have wallet options . This used to be the only way you could show a pic of your kid to a random person because no one had phones.” “Just paid $40 for my 6 year old’s soccer photos. I only ordered 8 trading cards, and he already had grass and mud stains on his uniform by the time we got to the photo area. … The digital would have been an additional $40.” “They didn’t even give us the option for an add on. Digital only came with the 70$ package. Just got the picture back today and it’s cute but they over corrected it so much it’s almost creepy” “The accuracy on this is insane” “The packages made sense for me when I was sending physical pictures to Great Grandma, but now she’s heaven side, I have more kids in school, and prices have gone UP. By the time I pay for each kids individual package, I might as well have just paid for family photos from a photographer that I picked out.” And yet, many parents still buy school portraits out of sentiment and tradition Interest has waned significantly over the years, especially with the rise of home digital photography on our phones and the rise in accessibility of family portraits. But despite it all, about 30% of families just can’t seem to quit buying these school photo packages. Even though the portraits often leave much to be desired and the packages are overpriced and horrifically outdated, the photos still have real sentimental value. There’s just something about putting all of the school portraits of your kids over the years together in one place, seeing the same pose, the same lighting, and the same backgrounds over and over. The only thing that changes is your kid, and it makes the passage of time incredibly visible and almost magical. View this post on Instagram In The Guardian , a photographer explains it well: “School photos might be a kind of flipbook; you can start in prep and rapidly watch your child age until they’re just BO and grunts. They’re not designed to be beautiful. Maybe they’re more like a war record.” They add, “The expectation is that this won’t be the best photo ever taken, but it will be my kid, in this moment, marking another year of their priceless life.” Parents can easily take their own photos or hire a photographer for a far more personalized family photo shoot. But the stock background and iconic portrait pose can really only be captured properly at the annual school session, so until we find another way to capture that moment in time, we’re stuck paying for more wallets and 8x10s than we know what to do with. And we’ll do it again next year. The post Parents are going off on the ‘robbery’ of school photo packages (and still buying them anyway) appeared first on Upworthy .

Ήθελε να συνεχίσει να ταξιδεύει. «Νομίζω ότι, αν δεν μπορώ να κάνω τα πράγματα που αγαπώ, δεν είναι…
items.descriptionOriginal: Stacy Hobson suffered from chronic kidney disease and high blood pressure and had been on the transplant list for 18 months. Her doctors told her the wait for a deceased donor kidney would run five to seven years, and that she should start dialysis. She said no. She wanted to keep traveling. “I’m like, if I can’t do the things that I love, it’s not living for me,” Hobson told Action News 5 . In May 2025, Hobson said she was in Greece when she suddenly felt at peace with whatever happened. That same month, about an hour and a half away in Memphis, Jenny Joyner started the testing process to give a kidney to someone she’d never met. Joyner has three kids: a high school senior, a middle child with Down syndrome, and a 10-year-old, as well as a job as an admissions counselor at Ole Miss. She hadn’t been planning any of this, but then a friend posted something on Facebook about living kidney donation, and she couldn’t stop thinking about it. View this post on Instagram “Facebook and God, to be honest,” she said, when asked how it started. “I could do that.” Then, she says, her husband set a drink down at dinner that night in a plastic cup with a transplant organization’s logo on it, one she didn’t recognize. “I didn’t even know we had the cup,” Joyner said. “It was like just another God piece into the story.” She spent weeks in compatibility testing at the Methodist Transplant Institute. Shortly after Hobson got home from Greece, her phone rang. “I literally screamed,” Hobson said. The surgery was in August 2025. Hospital privacy rules meant the two women still didn’t know each other’s names, so Hobson wrote a letter to the person who’d given her a kidney and sent it through the hospital. “I just thanked her from the bottom of my heart because I just feel there’s no amount of words that I could say to thank her enough,” Hobson said. Joyner read it while recovering at home, not knowing who had written it. The two met in early November, both fully recovered. Joyner says she’d do it again. More than 100,000 people are on the national transplant waiting list, and about 85 percent of them need a kidney. The post A Memphis woman faced years of waiting for a kidney. Then a complete stranger saw a Facebook post. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Τα ρομπότ της Κίνας σκαρφαλώνουν τα 3.100 βήματα του όρους Taishan πιο γρήγορα από τους ανθρώπους ορειβάτες
items.titleOriginal: China’s robots scale Mount Taishan’s 3,100 steps faster than human climbers
items.description: Η τεχνολογία ρομποτικής της Κίνας προχωρά με ταχείς ρυθμούς. Ένα εντυπωσιακό παράδειγμα αυτής της προόδου παρουσιάστηκε στην επαρχία Shandong στην ανατολική Κίνα, όπου πραγματοποιήθηκε ένας αναρριχητικός διαγωνισμός για ρομπότ στο όρος Taishan, ένα από τα πιο γνωστά βουνά της χώρας. items.descriptionOriginal: China’s robotics technology is advancing rapidly. A striking example of this progress was on display in Shandong Province in eastern China, where a climbing competition for robots was held on Mount Taishan, one of the country’s best-known mountains. The participating machines demonstrated their ability to negotiate difficult mountain paths, while also showcasing speed, balance and technical precision. Around 90 teams took part in the event, held on Monday. The teams represented major companies, universities and research institutions. The main course ran for approximately 3.9 kilometers, from Hongmen to Zhongtianmen on Mount Taishan. Tough terrain tackled for the race Along the route, the robots had to climb more than 3,100 steep stone steps and overcome an elevation gain of about 600 meters. The aim was not simply to test speed, but also to assess how effectively the machines could move across difficult and uneven terrain. Both humanoid robots and quadruped robots took part. Some moved cautiously, placing each step with care, while others appeared capable of climbing the stairs at a faster pace. A person typically takes around one and a half to two hours to complete the route on foot. The robots participating in the competition, however, completed it in less than an hour. According to China Central Television (CCTV) , a quadruped robot developed by Beijing Lingyi Technology, a wholly owned subsidiary of Hangzhou-based Unitree Robotics, secured first place in the race. It completed the course in 43 minutes and 41 seconds. Throughout the run, the robot continued across rough ground and narrow mountain paths, demonstrating its mobility and stability. The smallest quadruped robot in the competition was UNIUBI AI’s Cyvet. The company told the Global Times that, during a test, the robot autonomously covered the full route from Hongmen to Zhongtianmen in just 35 minutes and 47 seconds. To handle these challenges, the company equipped its quadruped robot with LiDAR technology. This allows the robot to scan its surroundings and distinguish between steps, rocks, and narrow passages. The system creates a 3D point-cloud map of the terrain, helping the robot identify a suitable path and navigate forward. The competition was not limited to speed. It also included tasks such as carrying loads, humanoid robot racing, and inspection in difficult environments. The Shandong company brought three different models to the event: two quadruped robots, the Y30 and E15, and one humanoid robot, the E1, which secured second place. The E1 humanoid robot developed by a Shandong-based robotics company also performed well, completing the route in 36 minutes and 18 seconds and securing second place in its category. The competition was broadly divided into two categories: speed races and specialized technical challenges. Four official events were organized under these categories. They included humanoid robot racing, load-carrying by legged robots, and mountain climbing with the assistance of exoskeletons. China’s robotics industry continues to expand According to the World Robotics 2026 report, China accounted for approximately three-fifths of the global share in 2025. Figures from China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology indicate that more than 400 humanoid robot models were available in the country and that over 40,000 units were produced in the first half of 2026. China’s robotics industry is also expanding rapidly, with continued work underway on industrial robots and humanoid machines. Xiang Ligang, president of the Beijing Institute of Intelligent Robot Industry, told the Global Times that robot competitions could become an indicator of technological progress, much as early exhibitions of aircraft and automobiles once captured public attention. According to Xiang, such competitions give robotics companies an opportunity to identify weaknesses in their technologies and make improvements. When robots from different companies operate in the same environment, their performance can also be compared more easily.

items.title: Ένας ηλικιωμένος άνδρας και μια γυναίκα χορεύουν με ποπ μουσική σε μια ρωμαϊκή πλατεία, δεν φαίνεται ένα βάζο με φιλοδωρήματα
items.titleOriginal: An old man and woman dance to pop music in a Roman piazza, not a tip jar in sight
items.description: Σε μια πλατεία στη Ρώμη, μια υπέροχη καλοκαιρινή βραδιά, ένα ηλικιωμένο δίδυμο έστησε ένα ηχείο και πάτησε «play». Το γνώριμο μπιτ και εισαγωγή της κιθάρας του "Beat It" του Μάικλ Τζάκσον γέμισαν τον αέρα και ο άνδρας και η γυναίκα άρχισαν να χορεύουν. Δεν χόρεψαν τυχαία, αλλά σε συνδυασμό με απλές χορογραφημένες χορευτικές κινήσεις. Δεν έχει ρυθμιστεί κάμερα. Χωρίς βάζο με άκρη. Μόλις δύο μεγαλύτερα It…
items.descriptionOriginal: In a piazza in Rome on a lovely summer evening, an elderly duo set up a speaker and pressed “play.” The familiar beat and guitar intro of Michael Jackson ‘s “Beat It” filled the air, and the man and woman began to dance . They didn’t dance randomly, but in unison with simple choreographed dance moves. No camera set up. No tip jar. Just two older Italians enjoying their evening in the piazza and bringing joy to themselves and others. The Tour Guy , a tour operator headquartered in Rome with tours across Europe, shared the delightful dance clip on Instagram, where it had been viewed more than five million times. View this post on Instagram They just wanted to dance The video was filmed on August 6, 2026, at approximately 7:00 p.m., by Sean Finelli . The caption of the video explained the scene: ⁠ “A man and a woman gathered in Piazza Testaccio, played Michael Jackson, and did a choreographed dance. They did this for about 20 mins to 5 or so different songs. Each dance was slightly different, but choreographed. They didn’t have a hat out to collect tips, they didn’t have anyone filming, they didn’t even want the video I took which I offered to share with them after, they just wanted to dance. ⁠ At the end, they walked in separate directions and that was it. I’ve been to this piazza almost daily the last two weeks and a few times per month this summer. I’ve never seen anyone do anything like this here. If you’re not familiar, Piazza Testaccio is one of the last remaining places in Rome where you can still find children playing each night and locals hanging out. The sense of community here is still strong.” A special moment in a special place Testaccio is a historically working-class Rome neighborhood built around the city’s ancient river port, and its name comes from the Latin word for the amphora shards that form Monte Testaccio . Some people in the comments concurred that Testaccio is something special:ng special: “I randomly came across this piazza one day and sat down to enjoy the shade, the children, the community. I was travelling alone and it was this beautiful moment of experiencing something not ‘for tourists.’ I spoke to no one, took no photos, so perhaps I got to blend in, just for a moment. ” Skyline of Rome, Italy. Photo credit: Canva “Best neighborhood, stayed there for a month was able to participate in the feste and pilgrimage around the neighborhood in May…l cant wait to return, love love loved it.” “I live nearby, when the good season starts they go to the park near Testaccio and dance for one hour or more, they practice a lot ! We love them.” Here for the vitality, not the virality People loved the carefree way the pair danced without any expectation of audience, virality, or recognition. “Congratulations to these two excellent dancers! So much beauty in this simple video.” “I love this! They’re doing it for their own happiness!” “How cute are they! This is what aging well looks like. Better than many young people. Congratulations to them. ” “Love this! They’re clearly living their best life doing what they enjoy ” “Looks like step aerobics. I love it. Still staying active and keeping it fresh. Italians are the best.” Meet Pasquale, the dancer People have wondered who the pair are. The man in the video showed up in the comments to thank everyone: “Hello everyone, I’m Pasquale, the gentleman in the video. THANK YOU to everyone for the kind words and for the affection shown .” (Pasquale has his own Instagram account . The description on his channel, translated from Italian, reads: “Music is part of my lifestyle; it thrills me, gives me strength, moves me… stimulates me.”) View this post on Instagram Someone else in the comments shared that Pasquale does a group dance class at the local senior center. What a wonderful way to stay vital and healthy in your golden years. (And for anyone wondering the status of the “couple,” someone else said they’re just friends.) Sometimes you just have to put some music and dance in the piazza, just for the fun of it. This article originally appeared in August. It has been updated. The post An old man and woman dance to pop music in a Roman piazza, not a tip jar in sight appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Ένας πλούσιος μαχαραγιάς πήρε 1.000 παιδιά από την Πολωνία κατά τη διάρκεια του Β' Παγκοσμίου Πολέμου, αναδημιουργώντας το σπίτι τους σε ινδικό έδαφος

items.description: Όταν εκατοντάδες Πολωνά παιδιά έφτασαν στην πολιτεία Nawanagar της Ινδίας (τώρα Jamnagar, στο Γκουτζαράτ) κατά τη διάρκεια του Β' Παγκοσμίου Πολέμου, είχαν ήδη εκδιωχθεί από τα σπίτια τους, είχαν επιζήσει από σοβιετικά στρατόπεδα εργασίας και ζούσαν χρόνια αβεβαιότητας. Ο πόλεμος είχε αφαιρέσει το σχολείο, τους φίλους και τις καθημερινές ρουτίνες που τα περισσότερα παιδιά χτίζουν φυσικά τη ζωή τους…
items.descriptionOriginal: When hundreds of Polish children arrived in India’s Nawanagar state (now Jamnagar, in Gujarat) during World War II , they had already been driven from their homes, survived Soviet labor camps, and lived through years of uncertainty . The war had stripped away school, friends, and the everyday routines most children naturally build their lives around. According to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum , the children’s journey had begun years earlier. Following the Soviet invasion of eastern Poland in 1939, about half a million Polish civilians were deported to labor camps in Siberia and Kazakhstan. After the 1941 Sikorski-Mayski Agreement allowed many Polish civilians to leave the Soviet Union, some eventually made the long journey through Iran to India. A portrait of Maharaja Jam Saheb Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji Jadeja, 1935. Photo credit: Bassano LTD/ Wikimedia Commons Creating a space to just be a kid again A July 2026 Smithsonian Magazine story recounts how Maharaja Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji Jadeja, the ruler of one of India’s princely states, Nawanagar, welcomed those children and created far more than a temporary refuge to wait out the war. Instead, he built a community where everyday life could begin again. There in Balachadi, nearly 1,000 children between the ages of 2 and 15 were given a safe place to stay from 1942 to 1946. A special camp was constructed near the maharaja’s summer palace on the Kathiawar Peninsula. The settlement included barracks, a school, a library, a Catholic church, kitchens, and places to play. The children returned to the classroom where Polish teachers continued lessons in their native language. Religious services and holidays like Christmas were observed much as they had before the war. Alongside food and shelter, the camp preserved familiar routines that helped restore a sense of normal life. Instead of wondering where they would sleep or where their next meal would come from, they worried about homework or raced across playing fields with new friends. He treated the children as his own children Wieslaw Stypula was only 11 years old when he joined the Balachadi community in 1942. In the 2013 documentary A Little Poland in India , Stypula recounted, “In this very grim scenario, I was adopted by people of a country I did not even know. It was here that I found happiness.” Digvijaysinhji called the children his own children. He would welcome new groups of Polish children, saying, “Do not consider yourself orphans any more. You are now Nawanagaris, and I am Bapu, father of all the people of Nawanagar, so also yours.” He was also dedicated to honoring their Polish identity. Anu Radha ,the filmmaker behind the documentary, told Smithsonian , “He insisted that every day, the Polish flag should be hoisted in the camp, and all children sing the Polish national anthem, in spite of the fatherland not being free.” The maharaja with kids and women from Poland. Alewis2388/ Wikimedia Commons Remarkable instincts without the modern humanitarian handbook Today, global relief organizations like UNICEF emphasize that children displaced by war need more than food and shelter . Education, opportunities to play, and cultural identity are all important parts of helping children recover from traumatic experiences. These ideas are reflected in UNICEF’s child-friendly spaces, which let children play, continue learning, and begin healing from trauma. They also echo a June 2026 statement from Save the Children for the International Day of Play, which says a safe place to play allows a child in conflict “to still hold on to part of their childhood.” For the children who arrived in Balachadi more than 80 years ago, the community the maharaja fostered became more than a refuge. It gave them the chance to be children again. The maharaja has not been forgotten. Warsaw has a Good Maharaja Square and schools named in his honor, and Poland posthumously awarded him the Commander’s Cross of the Order of Merit in 2011. When Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Warsaw in 2024, he paid tribute at a memorial to the maharaja and announced a youth exchange program named for the Jam Saheb, whose first group of 21 Polish youths later visited Jamnagar. This article originally appeared in August. It has been updated. The post A rich maharaja took in 1,000 Polish kids during WWII, recreating their home on Indian soil appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Εάν έχετε κάποια από αυτές τις 3 «κακές συνήθειες», μπορεί να σημαίνει ότι είστε πολύ έξυπνοι
items.titleOriginal: If you have any of these 3 ‘bad habits,’ it could mean you’re highly intelligent
items.description: Θα πίστευε κανείς ότι οι πολύ έξυπνοι άνθρωποι έχουν ευκολότερη ζωή. Όλη αυτή η εγκεφαλική δύναμη θα πρέπει να κάνει κάποιον πιο πειθαρχημένο, καλύτερο στη λήψη αποφάσεων και πιο επικεντρωμένο στη φροντίδα της ψυχικής του υγείας. Ωστόσο, το να έχεις έναν υπερδύναμο εγκέφαλο έρχεται με τα δικά του προβλήματα, όπως το να έχεις μια Ferrari θα σου φέρει περισσότερη θλίψη από το να έχεις ένα Toyot…
items.descriptionOriginal: One would think that highly intelligent people have easier lives. All that brainpower should make someone more disciplined, better at decision-making, and more focused on taking good care of their mental health. However, having a super-powered brain comes with its own problems, much like owning a Ferrari will give you more grief than owning a Toyota. Some people may be super smart but don’t really believe it because their lives aren’t exactly perfect and they still struggle with their faults and foibles. But that just means they’re human. In fact, highly intelligent people face challenges that aren’t necessarily solved by simply thinking their way out of them. Three ‘bad habits’ that super smart people often have Some research has linked these habits (that some folks deem “bad”) to higher scores on certain tests of ability. That doesn’t prove you’re highly intelligent, but it’s a good reason to go easy on yourself. 1. Smart people get bored easily Some researchers and educators have suggested that highly intelligent people get bored when forced to pFerform repetitive tasks or when activities are too easy. The evidence is mixed, though. A 2022 study of nearly 2,900 German third graders found that general cognitive ability was barely related to boredom, and that how interested students were in a subject mattered far more. However, there is some good news. People who enjoy thinking tend to seek out intellectual stimulation, which can help them find something interesting in a tedious task. Two students looking bored. Photo credit: Canva 2. Smart people swear a lot People often chastise those who use bad words for having a small vocabulary, which forces them to resort to vulgar language rather than find a more elegant way to express themselves. However, a 2015 study in Language Sciences found that people who could name more swear words in a minute also tended to name more non-swear words, which suggests that swearing fluency goes along with verbal fluency rather than a limited vocabulary. So, next time someone gives you grief for using colorful language, you can point out that it doesn’t mean you’re short on words. 3. Smart people stay up late A 2024 study from Imperial College London found that night owls, those who go to bed late, and early risers, those who get up early, scored differently on cognitive tests. The study drew on data from more than 26,000 UK Biobank participants. In two separate tests, night owls scored 13.5% and 7.5% higher than early risers. Those in the middle or “intermediate” types also scored higher than the early risers, by 10.6% and 6.3%. Why night owls may have an edge Night owls are often seen as lazy or undisciplined, so it may surprise some people that they scored higher on cognitive tests than those who go to bed early. The researchers noted that the study shows an association, not a cause, and that sleeping seven to nine hours a night was linked to the best brain function overall. It seems that at least part of the old adage, “Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise,” may not hold up. That doesn’t mean morning people are out of luck, though. The researchers noted that not all early risers perform worse. So, what does it all add up to? Ultimately, it seems that our assumptions about smart people aren’t all true. Many enjoy salty language, stay up late at night, and have a hard time paying attention if they aren’t being challenged. It goes to show that even though intelligence is a blessing, it doesn’t lead to a life that always looks perfect from the outside. And that if you struggle with staying focused, minding your language, or binge-watching late-night TV, it doesn’t mean you aren’t smart; in fact, it could be the exact opposite. This article originally appeared in July. It has been updated. The post If you have any of these 3 ‘bad habits,’ it could mean you’re highly intelligent appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Το απομακρυσμένο νησί όπου οι κάτοικοι μιλούν έναν συναρπαστικό συνδυασμό νότιων και παλαιών αγγλικών
items.titleOriginal: The remote island where residents speak a fascinating blend of Southern and Old English
items.description: Τα Αμερικάνικα Αγγλικά έρχονται σε όλα τα είδη διαφορετικών γεύσεων και ποικιλιών. Μεγάλωσα στη Βαλτιμόρη, η οποία μοιράζεται κάποιο διαλεκτικό DNA με την προφορά που βρίσκεις σε άλλες βορειοανατολικές πόλεις όπως η Φιλαδέλφεια. Baldamor, αγαπητέ! Υπάρχουν οι διάλεκτοι της Νέας Αγγλίας, με πιο γνωστή την προφορά της Βοστώνης: Pahk the cah στο Havahd yahd! Η προφορά της Νέας Υόρκης είναι παγκοσμίως γνωστή…
items.descriptionOriginal: American English comes in all sorts of different flavors and varieties. I grew up in Baltimore, which shares some dialectical DNA with the accent you find in other Northeastern cities like Philadelphia. Baldamor, hon! There are the New England dialects, most famously the Boston accent : Pahk the cah at Havahd yahd! The New York accent is world famous, as is the deep Southern twang, which gives way to a thick Cajun accent the closer you get to the bayous of Louisiana. These are all different versions of the greater American dialect . But there is one place, a tiny island off the coast of North Carolina, where a few residents speak in such a unique way that many listeners don’t even recognize it as American. Ocracoke, North Carolina, is home to a unique dialect called the Brogue, a blend of American Southern and English, Irish and Scottish influences from the 1600s. The Brogue, also known as Hoi Toider, is absolutely fascinating to hear in action. When you watch interviews with the locals of the island, they at first appear to be speaking a form of deep American Southern, and you can hear the twang the way you might in parts of Georgia or Alabama. But then, without warning, a word or phrase will slip out that sounds distinctly British. Centuries-old English, even. Then you’ll swear you hear a bit of Irish! How the Brogue took shape The dialect owes its roots to a surprising source: Pirates. Pirates loved to hide out on Ocracoke because the island is incredibly remote, roughly 20 miles from the mainland of North Carolina. Even today there are no bridges to Ocracoke and no scheduled commercial flights. Most visitors arrive by ferry, and some by private plane. Eventually, the island was purchased by William Howard, a man said to have served as Blackbeard’s quartermaster (yes, that Blackbeard), and his family helped build the settlement that followed. English sailors and Native American tribes also passed through and had their own unique impact on the culture and developing language of the island. In case you have your doubts about the island’s buccaneerish roots, there’s a popular legend about its name: “In one popular island legend, Ocracoke comes from the phrase, ‘Oh, crow cock,’ which was spoken by the infamous pirate Blackbeard as he waited to do battle at sunrise with the governor’s forces that had come to capture him,” writes a guide from NC State University. The dialect had a lot of room to develop without much outside influence. The BBC writes, “Howard’s community lived in near-isolation for almost two centuries. Electricity didn’t arrive at the island until 1938 and a ferry service didn’t start until 1957, leaving the islanders cut off except for the occasional supply trip to the mainland.” Words only locals would know That’s why Hoi Toider is still alive to this day, although its speaking population has dwindled to a few hundred people at most. Here are a few hallmark phrases of the unique dialect: A “dingbatter” is anyone not from the island, such as a tourist. An “O’cocker” is a native islander. “Meehonkey” is the island word for hide-and-seek. The Brogue uses ‘weren’t’ liberally for singular nouns (“The sun weren’t out yesterday.”) and frequently adds an ‘a’ in front of verbs (“We went a-fishin’ this morning”). But to fully appreciate Hoi Toider, you’ve got to hear it in action: Why the Brogue is slowly fading Experts say, as awesome as the Brogue is, it will likely disappear within the next 50 years. Though the island remains about as remote as it comes, there’s no escaping the influence of social media, television, and film these days. Every generation born on the island is a smidge less likely to adopt the Brogue than the one that came before. It will probably be mostly gone in the next couple of generations, which feels like a tragedy. Instead of “dingbatter” and “meehonkey,” the kids will be saying “rizz” and “no cap.” OK, maybe that’s an exaggeration, but young people growing up on the island won’t be as immersed in the language as their elders and will begin to speak more and more like your average American. There’s a concept called cultural homogenization . It’s the idea that over time, because of technology and globalization, unique individual cultures from around the world will all start to look more and more the same. It’s why you see fast food chains in the shadow of historic landmarks and people all over the globe listening to the same handful of musical artists. Ocracoke has managed to hang on longer than most places due to how difficult it is to reach. Here’s hoping that the Ocracoke Brogue can survive somehow, some way, in little pockets of the island. It’s just too dang cool and interesting to go away just yet. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post The remote island where residents speak a fascinating blend of Southern and Old English appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Μια γυναίκα μεγάλωσε χωρίς τη μαμά της. 21 χρόνια αργότερα, βρήκε το μυστικό της σημειωματάριο.
items.titleOriginal: A woman grew up without her mom. 21 years later, she found her secret notebook.
items.description: Κάποιοι από εμάς έχουμε την τύχη να θεωρούμε τους γονείς μας δεδομένους. Έχουμε έναν εγκέφαλο γεμάτο αναμνήσεις από αυτούς, και πολλές δεκαετίες για να δημιουργήσουμε νέες. Μαθαίνουμε ποιοι είναι ως άνθρωποι, ποιοι ήταν πριν γεννηθούμε, από πού κατάγονταν, ποιες ήταν οι ελπίδες και τα όνειρά τους, πώς γνώρισαν τον σύντροφό τους, τον άλλο γονιό μας. Μερικοί άνθρωποι δεν έχουν αυτή την πολυτέλεια. Accor…
items.descriptionOriginal: Some of us are lucky enough to take our parents for granted. We have a brain full of memories of them, and many decades to form new ones. We learn who they are as people, who they were before we were born, where they came from, what their hopes and dreams were, how they met their partner, our other parent. Some people don’t have that luxury . According to Judi’s House, about 1 in 11 U.S. children will experience the death of a parent or sibling by age 18. A woman named Blakelyn suffered unimaginable tragedy as a child when both of her parents died in separate car accidents within a few years of each other. She grew up hungry for any tangible memories of what they were like. Blakelyn’s mother died when she was just 6 months old, according to Newsweek. She grew up with no mother, very little understanding of what happened, and almost no memories of her. Worse, her father was too grief-stricken to talk much about Blakelyn’s mom, understandably so. That left her very little to go on, and when he sadly passed away too, she lost the only connection she had to her mother. A journal nobody knew existed Imagine her shock when, 21 years later, Blakelyn’s aunt discovered an old journal belonging to her mom while sorting through rooms at Blakelyn’s grandparents’ house. Blakelyn was desperate to get her hands on it and captured her reaction to its contents in a powerful post on social media. What was inside her mom’s journal For the first time in her life, Blakelyn got a look inside her mom’s heart and mind. And she uncovered some amazing revelations along the way. Among the highlights of the journal are pages and pages of notes Blakelyn’s mom made as she was brainstorming names for her baby girl. There are lists of first names, first-and-middle-name pairings, and experiments with different combinations. In the post, Blakelyn expresses awe that her name was almost Baylee Alyssa, and also Bailey Alana. Mom had really honed in on those creative B names! In a calendar portion of the journal, Mom noted key dates like the day she moved in with Blakelyn’s dad, and also the day he proposed. Blakelyn had never known that the two were engaged when her mom died. Mom also crossed off dates in succession, counting down the days until her daughter was born. It was all overwhelming in the best way. @itspurplehead Replying to @iliana i don’t have many but i cherish the ones i do have ♬ Take My Hand – Matt Berry The TikToker told Newsweek that not having any memories of her mom didn’t make the loss any less painful. In a way, it left her searching for this intangible missing piece her entire life. Now, with the journal, she’s got that piece back. Why viewers couldn’t stop crying The post went viral, racking up hundreds of thousands of likes and bringing viewers to tears, as shared in the comments: “She LOVED you. She wanted the most perfect name for you. She LOVED you. SHE LOVED YOU” “you were so loved BEFORE you were here. imagine how much more they love you after they are gone … i’m sorry luv. you were seriously her most prized possession!!” “She was just a girl, and she loved you and thought of you so much before you were even born” “Wait, I love that she used the calendar to write the good things that happened versus using it to plan out future events. How sweet!” “This is so sweet. Both of my parents passed away and a few months ago I found their love letters they had written to each other while they were long distance before I was even born. I tell myself all the time they were just teenagers in love.” A few commenters even had a great idea. Now that Blakelyn has her own name in her mom’s handwriting, she’s got all the makings of an epic and emotional tattoo, a way to carry a piece of her mom with her everywhere. Blakelyn responded to the idea in the comments: “I definitely will be doing this.” This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post A woman grew up without her mom. 21 years later, she found her secret notebook. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Η πρώτη μεγάλη αναδρομική έκθεση της Μαρίκο Μόρι στην Ιαπωνία από το 2002 εγκαινιάστηκε στο Μουσείο Τέχνης Μόρι στο Τόκιο δομημένη ως μια καθηλωτική διαδρομή μέσα από τρεις δεκαετίες καλλιτεχνικής πρακτικής. Η έκθεση «Mariko Mori: All That Shines» συνεργασία του Μουσείου Τέχνης Μόρι σε συνεργασία με το Ίδρυμα Σόλομον Ρ. Γκούγκενχαϊμ περιλαμβάνει 40 έργα που καλύπτουν περισσότερες από τρεις δεκαετίες και παρουσιάζει τις καλλιτεχνικές και εννοιολογικές καινοτομίες της καλλιτέχνιδας σε όλα τα μέσα που αποτελούν σήμα κατατεθέν της: φωτογραφία και βίντεο (βασισμένα στην περφόρμανς ή στην ψηφιακή επεξεργασία), σχέδιο, γλυπτική και διαδραστικές εγκαταστάσεις μεγάλης κλίμακας. Διαβάστε περισσότερα Στα μέσα της δεκαετίας του 1990 η Μαρίκο Μόρι αναδείχθηκε σε εμβληματική μορφή της εποχής, μαγνητίζοντας τον κόσμο της τέχνης με τη σειρά έργων της «Cyborg» -φωτογραφίες και βίντεο που βασίζονται στην περφόρμανς- καθώς και με εικόνες εμπνευσμένες από την επιστημονική φαντασία, οι οποίες αξιοποιούν προηγμένα γραφικά υπολογιστή. Έκτοτε, το ενδιαφέρον της διευρύνθηκε: από την κριτική προσέγγιση της σύγχρονης κοινωνίας -με θεματικές όπως η ιαπωνική κουλτούρα των anime, το φύλο και ο μετα-ανθρωπισμός- στράφηκε προς ευρύτερους μεταφυσικούς προβληματισμούς, επηρεασμένους σε μεγάλο βαθμό από βουδιστικές αντιλήψεις για τη ζωή, τον θάνατο και το σύμπαν, σύμφωνα με την περιγραφή της έκθεσης. Διαβάστε περισσότερα Μεγαλώνοντας στα προάστια του Τόκιο τη δεκαετία του 1970 η καλλιτέχνιδα διατηρεί ευχάριστες αναμνήσεις από τη δημοφιλή σειρά επιστημονικής φαντασίας «Astro Boy» και όταν έπαιζε με τους φίλους της, αναρωτιώταν πώς θα μπορούσε να είναι το μέλλον, φαντάζονταν διαφορετικούς κόσμους. Η Μαρίκο Μόρι εξακολουθεί να φαντάζεται εναλλακτικές πραγματικότητες και να προσκαλεί τους θεατές σε αυτούς τους κόσμους που η ίδια δημιουργεί. Από την εξερεύνηση των βαθύτερων επιπέδων της ανθρώπινης συνείδησης μέσω της τεχνολογίας, έως την απόδοση τιμής σε προϊστορικούς τόπους διαφόρων πολιτισμών, το έργο της μάς προσκαλεί να στοχαστούμε πάνω σε όσα μας ενώνουν. Η έκθεση «Mariko Mori: All That Shines» εγκαινιάστηκε στις 31 Οκτωβρίου και θα διαρκέσει έως τις 28 Μαρτίου 2027. items.descriptionOriginal: Happy Eco News Endangered Animals Making a Comeback in 2027 Reading Time: 4 minutes Endangered Animals Making a Comeback in 2027 When you hear about endangered wildlife, it’s often another story of shrinking habitats, declining populations or species facing extinction. However, there is good news worth celebrating, too. Thanks to dedicated conservation efforts, some of the world’s most threatened animals are making remarkable comebacks. From mountain gorillas thriving in protected forests to bald eagles soaring across North America, you’ll find encouraging examples of how conservation can reverse population declines. Discover inspiring wildlife recovery stories that offer hope to endangered animals and show how your support for conservation can make a difference. 1. Mountain Gorillas Decades of habitat protection, veterinary care and anti-poaching initiatives have helped mountain gorilla populations grow to over 1,000 individuals , with multiple family groups. It’s a significant improvement for a species that once faced a much bleaker future. You’ll find these great apes in two isolated regions of Central and East Africa, where conservation teams work alongside local communities to protect the remaining habitat. The survival of this primate species extends beyond the gorillas themselves. Protecting large primates can also preserve entire ecosystems. While mountain gorillas remain endangered, their growing numbers demonstrate the value of long-term conservation. Expanding these efforts to other primate species may also protect smaller endangered species. 2. Bald Eagles Few wildlife recoveries are as impressive as that of the bald eagle. Once threatened by hunting, habitat destruction and the irresponsible use of the pesticide commonly known as DDT, America’s national bird has made an extraordinary species comeback. DDT led to poor-quality egg production, making successful breeding incredibly difficult for bald eagles. The ban on DDT, stronger legal protections and habitat conservation helped reverse decades of population decline. According to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the population in the lower 48 states increased from approximately 72,434 birds in 2009 to just over 316,000 birds , with 71,467 breeding pairs tracked between 2018 and 2019. Today, you’ll see bald eagles near rivers, lakes and coastlines across much of North America. Their remarkable recovery shows how environmental laws and sustained conservation efforts can give threatened wildlife a second chance. 3. Sea Turtles For sea turtles, the journey to adulthood begins with a dangerous dash from nest to ocean. Fortunately, conservation programs are giving more hatchlings a fighting chance through beach patrols, nest monitoring and community involvement. In the Philippines, conservationists have even recruited four-legged helpers. Project CURMA’s Paw Patrol uses specially trained dogs to sniff out buried turtle eggs , allowing volunteers to locate and protect nests from poachers and other threats. Efforts to reduce accidental catches in fishing nets, restore nesting beaches and limit artificial lighting along the coastlines are helping protect sea turtles at different stages of their lives. Some populations have shown encouraging improvements following decades of protection. While several sea turtle species remain endangered or critically endangered, initiatives like these show that creative conservation strategies can improve their chances of survival. When you participate in community initiatives, such as Paw Patrol, you increase the support that struggling species need to survive. 4. Tigers Tigers have lost much of their historical range to deforestation, human development and poaching. However, conservation efforts in parts of Asia are helping these magnificent predators reclaim lost ground. Wild tigers live across parts of Asia, where conservation efforts have helped some populations rebound after the global population fell to an estimated 3,200 in 2010. India offers one of the strongest examples, as it is now home to about 70% of the world’s wild tigers. Forest conservation has played a valuable part in this and other success stories. Sustainable forestry and other interventions have slowed global deforestation rates by almost 40% since the 1990s, which is why purchasing sustainably sourced timber is so important, whether you buy new floors, furniture or even musical instruments. Habitat loss remains a threat, but support for responsible forest management offers hope. 5. American Alligators American alligators were once hunted so extensively for their valuable skins that their survival became a serious concern. By 1967, the species had gained federal endangered status, prompting stronger protections against hunting and illegal trade. Conservation measures, including regulated harvesting and wetland management, helped restore their numbers. The species was removed from the U.S. endangered species list in 1987, just two decades after receiving protection. Today, up to 1.06 million mature American alligators inhabit the southeastern United States. With the species now classified as least concern, you’re looking at one of America’s most successful wildlife recovery stories. 6. Other Stories of Recovery The good news continues across the world. Other threatened species are showing encouraging signs of recovery, giving you even more reasons to feel hopeful about wildlife conservation. The Iberian lynx has rebounded from near extinction, thanks to captive breeding and habitat restoration across Spain and Portugal. North Atlantic right whales are also showing tentative signs of population growth, although their survival remains precarious. Meanwhile, giant pandas have benefited from decades of habitat protection and breeding programs, while southern white rhinos have recovered significantly from historical population lows through intensive conservation efforts. Humpback whales offer another success story, with several populations rebounding after commercial whaling restrictions gave these ocean giants a chance to recover. These achievements highlight the importance of patience and persistence, as rebuilding wildlife populations often requires decades of protection and ongoing monitoring. Every contribution makes a difference, and even keeping your distance from these animals, respecting protected habitats and choosing ethical wildlife tourism experiences contribute to various species’ success stories. Why Are More Endangered Animals Recovering? Wildlife recovery rarely happens by chance. Behind these success stories are years of coordinated conservation efforts, scientific research and communities working to protect vulnerable species. These efforts also benefit entire ecosystems. When you protect forests, wetlands and oceans, you’re helping preserve the habitats that countless species depend on for survival. Several approaches are helping endangered animals rebuild their populations: Habitat protection: National parks, wildlife corridors and sustainable land management give animals safer places to live, breed and find food. Stronger wildlife laws: Hunting restrictions, anti-poaching patrols and international trade regulations help reduce human-driven threats. Breeding and reintroduction programs: Conservationists can raise threatened animals in protected environments and then release them into suitable habitats where they have a better chance of thriving. Community involvement: Local conservation projects encourage people to protect wildlife while supporting livelihoods through responsible tourism and sustainable practices. Scientific monitoring: Tools like GPS collars, population surveys, and genetic research help conservationists spot problems earlier and celebrate progress when recovery efforts work. A Brighter Future for Endangered Wildlife Every species making a comeback represents years of dedication and a reminder that extinction isn’t always inevitable. Although many endangered animals still face serious threats, these conservation successes show that meaningful progress is possible. You can help sustain that momentum by supporting wildlife conservation organizations, choosing responsibly sourced products and spreading awareness about threatened species. Even small actions contribute to a broader movement to protect biodiversity. With continued commitment, today’s recovery stories could become tomorrow’s thriving wildlife populations.
